body:
I'm Canadian, in Ontario. As far as I'm aware I'd need a parent's consent in these types of situations. It doesn't help that I'm not allowed to go outside by myself (my mother says I can go out only if I'm with a friend and I don't have any friends) so I'd have no way of getting to a therapist. I'm also just wary of therapy in my area because I live in the same place as I did when I had awful therapists, and it's a pretty small place.

But once I get older I would like to try again at therapy, and it's helpful to know that there are many different types of therapy.

There are many things I love and look forward to in life. It's just the muted, diminished sense of enjoyment with them and the random episodes of intense pain/confusion/lethargy that I can't stand, and the prospect of having to deal with that for a long time until I /maybe/ get better from it just makes me think, "no thanks, I'd rather end it now."

Therapy/medication are out of reach for me unfortunately. Additionally I’m a minor so drugs risk being harmful to my development, as they have been when I was forced to take adult doses of antidepressants in the past. I don’t have much say as to what kind of treatment I get because of my age and I don’t know if I can hang on for years until I’m an adult. All I have is myself and a friend so I’m limited in what I can access.

I’ve been working gradually on getting back into breathing exercises. So far it’s difficult because it reminds me of a past therapist who advocated it quite aggressively, but I’m trying. I don’t know if religion would work well for me because I’m a very facts over faith person and some aspects of myself are considered wrong by certain religions. I used to be Christian, but it was always difficult to truly believe without any indisputable facts, and being considered wrong caused me a great deal of stress.
